I have farmed these 6.5 mu in Quzhou for 43 years. I finished middle school, and I pick up new ideas from the input dealer in town and from watching my neighbors. My household has five people, but my son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so most days it is just me and my wife in the fields. I hire two workers for three days at wheat harvest because we cannot manage the cutting and hauling alone.

I keep 5 mu for the wheat-maize rotation and 1.5 mu for chili. I do not change my system much because change is risky. Last year fertilizer prices were high, but a bad harvest is a disaster while extra fertilizer is only money lost. I would rather sleep soundly knowing I fed my crops enough.

For wheat this winter, I sow the improved variety that everyone in my village uses, about 15 kg of seed per mu. Before sowing I rotary till. I spread one 50 kg bag of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu as base, which gives 8 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. At green-up I top-dress 20 kg urea per mu, and another 20 kg urea at jointing. That adds about 18 kg nitrogen, so the wheat gets about 26 kg nitrogen per mu in total. I irrigate three times from my well: before the freeze, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray herbicide once after sowing and fungicide once at heading because there was rust on the next field last year. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize on the same 5 mu, I use hybrid seed at 2 kg per mu. Right after wheat harvest I rotary till and sow immediately. I put down one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base, then 35 kg urea per mu at big trumpet stage. That is about 24 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, at sowing if it is dry and at tasseling. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide early, then insecticide for corn borer. I expect 650 kg per mu. The seed dealer claims 700 kg, but I never count on the dealer's numbers.

For chili on the 1.5 mu, I plant hybrid seedlings in early May after rotary tilling in April. I use one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base. At flowering I add 15 kg urea and 20 kg potassium sulfate per mu, because chili needs potassium or the fruits are small and thin-skinned. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 18 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate four times, especially during fruit set. I spray pesticide four times. Last year my neighbor Wang sprayed only twice and the worms ruined half his crop. I learned from his mistake. I expect 2500 kg of fresh chili per mu.

My total spending on fertilizer will be about 3200 yuan, pesticide about 900 yuan, and hired labor 500 yuan. The off-farm income covers family costs, but the farm must pay for itself. If money runs short, I might delay buying new boots, but I will not cut fertilizer or pesticide because that is gambling with the harvest. I watch what my neighbors do, and if they all add more urea this spring, I will add more too. Copying a successful neighbor is safer than guessing.
